annotation_description: Cavern of Souls was named 'Avatar' but Bringer of the Last Gift is a Vampire Demon, not an Avatar. The two Superior Spider-Man cards are Spider Human Hero creatures. By naming Avatar, the Cavern of Souls can't produce colored mana for any creature in hand and its 'can't be countered' clause won't apply to anything relevant. Naming 'Human' or 'Spider' would have covered the two Superior Spider-Man copies, and naming 'Vampire' or 'Demon' would have covered Bringer of the Last Gift.

Playing Multiversal Passage costs 2 life to enter untapped when a basic Mountain would enter untapped for free and accomplish the same thing (enabling Fear of Missing Out cast this turn). Multiversal Passage should be saved for a later turn when its flexibility is more valuable.

Fear of Missing Out's enter-the-battlefield trigger requires discarding a card then drawing a card. Discarding Boomerang Basics (a sorcery) adds a sorcery type to the graveyard, which helps enable Delirium (4+ card types in graveyard). However, Boomerang Basics is a useful tempo/removal spell that can bounce opposing threats. The player could have discarded a land instead (like Riverpyre Verge or Mountain, since they already have Spirebluff Canal and Multiversal Passage plus will draw a card). Discarding a land would add the land type to graveyard for Delirium while preserving the more flexible spell. That said, discarding Boomerang Basics does add a sorcery type which may be harder to get otherwise, and the player may value having more land drops. This is debatable.

Cast Oblivious Bookworm before making a land drop on turn 3. By playing a land first (e.g., Starting Town, which enters untapped on turn 3, or Overgrown Tomb paying 2 life), the player would have 3 mana available after casting the 2-mana Bookworm, leaving mana open. Playing spells before lands is a sequencing error that reduces flexibility.

Playing Overgrown Tomb (paying 2 life to enter untapped) when Starting Town would enter untapped for free on turn 3 and produce the same colors needed this turn. Starting Town only costs 1 life for colored mana vs 2 life for Overgrown Tomb entering untapped.

GPT4om Stoic cast Fear of Missing Out before playing a land for the turn. They have multiple lands in hand (Island, Riverpyre Verge, Steam Vents, Mountain, Spirebluff Canal) and should play a land first to ensure they don't miss a land drop. More importantly, Fear of Missing Out's enter-the-battlefield trigger requires discarding a card then drawing - by casting it before playing a land, they risk discarding a land they could have played, or they lose flexibility in choosing what to discard since they haven't committed to a land drop yet. Additionally, casting a creature before combat when you already have a Fear of Missing Out on the battlefield is slightly questionable - though there's no combat trick concern here. The main issue is sequencing: land should come before spells.

Discarded Mountain instead of the second Spirebluff Canal. With 2 lands already in play, any future Spirebluff Canal would enter tapped (requires 2 or fewer other lands), making it strictly worse than a basic Mountain which always enters untapped. Mountain provides red mana just like Spirebluff Canal would.

Opponent has zero creatures on the battlefield, making attacking with all creatures completely free. By only attacking with one Fear of Missing Out (2 damage), GPT4om Stoic left 5 additional damage on the table (second FoMO for 2 + Tiger-Seal for 3 with vigilance so it stays untapped).

Casting Formidable Speaker before playing a land is a sequencing error. Haiku Libby has Overgrown Tomb and Starting Town in hand, and should play a land first to have 4 mana available. With 4 mana, they could potentially cast Formidable Speaker and still have mana open, or play the land untapped (Starting Town on turn 4 enters tapped, but Overgrown Tomb could enter untapped for 2 life). More importantly, playing the land first is free and preserves options - for instance, if Formidable Speaker's ETB trigger lets them discard and tutor, having the extra land on board could matter for subsequent plays. Additionally, casting creatures before combat is generally suboptimal when you have nothing to gain from it pre-combat, though here the opponent has a tapped Fear of Missing Out and Tiger-Seal (which taps on upkeep) so combat isn't particularly relevant.

message: Discard a card and search your library for a creature card, reveal it, put it into your hand, then shuffle?
annotation_description: Discarded Oblivious Bookworm, a strong card advantage engine, instead of a redundant second Superior Spider-Man. Spider-Man is legendary, so only one can be on the battlefield at a time, making the second copy less valuable. Bookworm provides ongoing card draw which would help find lands and gas. The player also incorrectly believed they already had a Bookworm in play.

Casting Stormchaser's Talent before playing a land drop is a sequencing error. GPT4om Stoic has three lands in hand (Riverpyre Verge, Steam Vents, Spirebluff Canal) and should play a land first before casting spells. Playing a land first costs nothing and preserves information — you might want to hold the Talent depending on what develops. More importantly, the Otter token created by Stormchaser's Talent has prowess, so casting spells after the token enters would trigger prowess and pump it. By casting the Talent now (before combat), the token won't benefit from any prowess triggers this turn unless additional spells are cast. However, with only 1 untapped mana remaining after casting Talent (Island), there's limited ability to cast more spells. The land-before-spell sequencing is the main issue.

Chose Jeskai (draw on combat damage) over Temur (+1/+0, trample, haste) when opponent has no creatures and is at 12 life. Temur would add +1 power to each creature per combat, which compounds with Fear of Missing Out's extra combat phases. Against an empty board, the extra damage from Temur likely closes the game faster than drawing 1 card per combat phase.

Spirebluff Canal enters tapped with 4+ other lands, while Steam Vents could enter untapped (for 2 life). Since both lands will be available eventually, the question is whether having an extra untapped mana this turn is worth 2 life. With two Fear of Missing Out on board ready to attack and potential need for mana flexibility this turn, playing Steam Vents untapped might be slightly preferable.

Discarded Requiting Hex, a 1-mana removal spell that can kill Tiger-Seal (3/3 vigilance), Fear of Missing Out, or Otter Token, while at 6 life facing an aggressive board. This is one of the most immediately impactful and castable cards in hand.

Leveled up Stormchaser's Talent before playing a land. Should have played Island or Steam Vents first to have more mana available after the level-up, potentially allowing them to cast the recovered spell (Torch the Tower) in the same turn or hold up Spell Snare. With the opponent at 6 life, having Torch the Tower plus combat damage could be lethal this turn.

GPT4om Stoic cast Boomerang Basics (a sorcery costing {U}) before playing a land for the turn. They have Steam Vents and Island in hand. Playing a land first (Island, which enters untapped for free) would preserve mana options and is strictly better sequencing. Additionally, Boomerang Basics returns a nonland permanent to its owner's hand - if targeting their own permanent they draw a card, but if targeting an opponent's permanent they don't. With the opponent at 6 life and GPT4om having two Fear of Missing Out and combat creatures, the question is whether Boomerang Basics is even the right play here versus developing the board. However, bouncing one of the opponent's lands or setting up for combat could be reasonable. The main issue is casting a spell before playing a land drop.
